title: SDK integration walkthrough - Evergreen Commerce
summary: AE+SE walked through Redwood SDK quickstarts in Python and TypeScript, auth patterns (API key vs SSO), env setup, and a short Console tour. Customer wants a pilot with Dedicated capacity and SSO; action items include sharing pricing, security whitepaper, and scheduling a benchmark run.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro i'm maya, i'm the AE on the Evergreen account. jordan from engineering is with me — jordan, say hi?
[00:08] Jordan Kim: hey all, jordan kim, solutions engineer, we'll do a short SDK walkthrough and then demos in the console and touch on optimize.
[00:16] Lina Morales: hi all, lina here — sorry running a bit late, thanks for setting this up.
[00:20] Maya Patel: no problem, we have about 45 minutes, plan is quick context, then python + typescript quickstart, auth patterns, show console for routing/optimize, then next steps. sound good?
[00:32] Samir Patel: yep good. we're mainly evaluating for checkout chat and product search embeddings, latency requirements 150-200 ms p95 for chat in EU region, and strict data residency.
[00:45] Jordan Kim: good note on latency and residency — we'll cover dedicated vs hosted and our private options. first quickstart, python. install pip install redwood-inference (note sometimes pkg name is redwood-sdk in older docs, ignore). code snippet:
[00:58] Jordan Kim: from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
response = client.chat.create(model='redwood-1-large', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}])
print(response.text)
[01:20] Ava Chen: couple quick q's, do you support service account keys or short-lived tokens? we rotate keys frequently.
[01:25] Jordan Kim: yes both — long-lived API keys for quickstarts, and we recommend short-lived tokens for prod via our auth exchange; also SAML/SSO for user management and RBAC. we can provide a sample flow with our oauth proxy or show how to mint tokens in the Dedicated control plane.
[01:40] Maya Patel: for env setup, we suggest secrets manager for REDWOOD_API_KEY and the region: REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west-1 will hit our eu edge. for private deployments you'll point the SDK at a private endpoint, e.g. REDWOOD_API_URL=https://private.redwood.example (placeholder).
[01:55] Jordan Kim: typescript quickstart looks like: npm i @redwood-inference/sdk
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const r = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1-large', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] })
console.log(r.text)
[02:20] Samir Patel: any recommended timeouts and retry strategies? we have intermittent spikes.
[02:24] Jordan Kim: set short per-request timeout 5s for reads, and use exponential backoff with jitter; SDKs have a built-in retry util if you enable it. batching is supported in the embeddings client to reduce cost, and continuous KV cache for chat to speed up repeated prefixes.
[02:40] Lina Morales: can you explain optimize recommendations — batching/quantization caching?
[02:45] Jordan Kim: sure keep in mind tradeoffs — quantization reduces memory/cost but may change output slightly; our Optimize tool will run a profile and recommend a quantization profile per model. caching (prefix/KV) is big for assistant workloads where many requests share the same opening prompt. autoscaling and routing policies can route to cheaper model variants for low priority traffic.
[03:10] Maya Patel: security — do you have SOC 2 & ISO? how are logs handled?
[03:15] Jordan Kim: yes SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001; we provide audit logs and per-tenant encryption options. for private on-prem deployments you keep keys in your KMS/HSM. we'll share the security whitepaper and our compliance pack.
[03:30] Ava Chen: how does SSO integrate with Dedicated? we need SCIM and SAML.
[03:32] Jordan Kim: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC; can map roles to routes and model access. for Dedicated customers we can manage the IdP integration in the tenant control plane.
[03:45] Samir Patel: about model variants and fallback — if our primary model is busy will there be auto fallback?
[03:49] Jordan Kim: yes you can have smart routing policies: primary model, fallback variant (smaller quantized) and region fallback. you can specify latency or cost as policy. these are configured in the console per route.
[04:05] Maya Patel: quick console tour — sharing screen now — show logs, per-route dashboards, traces, cost by token, the rollout UI for canaries. (screen noises)
[04:20] Jordan Kim: here's how you create an API key in console for dev, and how you create a service account for CI with scoped permissions. remember to restrict keys to routes to limit blast radius.
[04:36] Lina Morales: question, does the SDK support streaming? we need streaming responses for chat UI.
[04:40] Jordan Kim: yes python and typescript both support streaming; sample uses an async iterator in TS and a generator in python. caveat: streaming telemetry behaves slightly differently behind a proxy, we'll include sample code.
[04:55] Ava Chen: any gotchas with proxies and private networks?
[04:58] Jordan Kim: proxies fine as long as you allow websocket or chunked transfer; for on-prem we usually configure an ingress with sticky sessions and adjust timeouts. sometimes customers hit TLS inspection rules that break websockets so be mindful.
[05:15] Samir Patel: on pricing, is there a difference for Dedicated?
[05:18] Maya Patel: yes Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit — different pricing model, plus options for burst and overage. we'll send a pricing sheet.
[05:26] Lina Morales: ok next steps from our side: we'd like a short pilot, we need SSO review with our security team, and a benchmark run in our eu region with sample traffic.
[05:36] Maya Patel: perfect — we'll do that. any other questions?
[05:40] Ava Chen: small nit, docs sometimes refer to "redwood optimize" as RedwoodOptimize, small inconsistencies — just FYI.
[05:50] Jordan Kim: noted, docs team is iterating on that, thanks.
[05:55] Maya Patel: recap: we will send pricing and Dedicated SLA, security whitepaper and SSO integration guide; jordan will provide sample benchmark harness and quickstart repo links. lina, samir, ava you will confirm pilot scope and security contacts and propose pilot dates.
[06:12] Samir Patel: sounds good, aiming for a pilot start in two weeks.
[06:20] Maya Patel: great, we'll follow up via email, thanks everyone.
[06:24] Lina Morales: thanks all. bye.
[06:28] End of recording
